claim: `BACKLOG.md` is the live canonical list of pending CAS MergeTree work, while `ROADMAP.md` is the DONE/history roll-up.
In `ca-fsck` vocabulary, `dangling` means referenced but missing and is the INV-NO-LOSS data-loss class, whereas `unreachable`/`awaiting-gc` means present, unreferenced, and awaiting reclamation.

The unmatched-minus-one retention leak left 56 blobs with exactly one residual source edge whose manifest no longer existed; the edges traced to four `tmp-fetch_*` refs published and dropped within 43 ms.
Queueing an exact removal is not a valid fix for the unmatched-minus-one leak because `RefTableState` throws `CORRUPTED_DATA` when the binding is absent, turning the leak into a permanent wedge.
The flat 180-second fsck budget can time out once the ref space is large enough that the check for stuck blobs stops running at the scale where it is needed.
Across 1,673 GC rounds, `fold_ref_intake` was linear in the ref-log backlog and sustained 256 logs per second.
The flat cost of ref intake was approximately 0.92 ms per request rather than per log, and requests per log ranged from 2.5 to 4.7 and increased with backlog size.
`orphan_sweep` had the worst median duration at 383 ms per round, while `lease` was approximately 2 ms at p50 across 2,255 rounds.
GC advanced its fold cursor over records merely observed in a paginated LIST without a completeness proof, creating the LIST-as-journal deletion hole tracked as a release blocker.
The LIST-as-journal detector had fired 14 times but still needed lease identity recorded at both ends of the enumeration to distinguish an actual listing hole from concurrent deletion.

The rev.6 ref protocol made writer exclusivity a mount-lease handover property using an unclean-handover wait, a `released_clean` fast path, an eager recovery-snapshot seal, and publish-from-live snapshots; the later v9 in-band `EpochSeal` retired `materialization_grace_ms`/`T_mat`.
The v9 in-band `EpochSeal` landed as the fix for the cross-epoch late-materialization hazard in which a fenced predecessor PUT could materialize below successor snapshot coverage.

`claimMount` can reclaim a same-UUID body marked `gc_fenced`, clean-marked, or proven-dead without comparing epochs, potentially allowing a fresh writer with a lower `writer_epoch` than the reclaimed body's epoch; the effect on `prev_epoch_seal` obligations remains undecided.

The ref-snapshot/log Phase 2 optimization candidates include indexed or chunked snapshots, lazy snapshot blocks, a bounded row cache, a per-round ref index, decoded-body reuse, and chunked namespace removal.

`CasRequestController` provides single-attempt conditional writes, a budget, fence gating, and exact-key resolution for the ref lane, but `promoteStaged`'s `copyObjectConditional` is a separate retry mechanism and `casPutObject`/`casRemoveObject` still use the disk default retry policy.

Trusted-LIST frontier mode may skip the exact `GET cursor+1` probe only for a per-backend certified store whose LIST is known to include keys completed before the LIST began; the mode must remain opt-in and fail closed to probe-always.

The middle of a ref-log enumeration remains arithmetic on every backend because predecessor omission below a correct paginated LIST tail is legal under concurrent writes; held namespaces and namespaces with no listed logs must still use the probe.
RustFS failed the LIST-consistency passport by omitting keys that had been durable for 19 seconds, so conservative probe-always behavior remains the default.

A backend-independent parallel exact-key walk can fan out namespace probes and `cursor+1..tail` record GETs over a bounded pool without changing the trust model, while fold application remains ordered or deterministic.
The dominant remaining hot-pool byte cost is rewriting the full snapshot run in O(edges) per pass; the proposed remedy is O(delta)-write log-structured runs with periodic compaction.
Measured GC round cost grew with pool size from 87 ms at 400 parts to 93 s at 10,000 tables and 398 s at 100,000 parts.
Incremental point-updatable in-degree is intended to make non-idle small-delta rounds O(delta) and provide a global change signal that can eliminate the per-round `LIST(cas/refs/)` O(shards) sweep.
The proposed adaptive GC cadence keys folding on per-shard journal pressure by size or age rather than changed-shard count, with a pool-specific `gc_interval_sec` direction of roughly 30–60 seconds.
Part removal generated 17,707 `ref_repoint` events, all on `delete_tmp_*` refs, costing approximately 53,000 PUTs or 22% of the writer PUT class in the measured soak.
Empty-shard GC probes caused approximately 1,174 `DiskS3ReadRequestsErrors` per round, growing by about four per round as new shards were touched.
Insert queries accumulated 339.6 seconds of `CasRefQueueWaitMicroseconds` over 7,131 inserts, or approximately 48 ms of ref-lane queue wait per insert on average.

A long or wedged GC round currently becomes visible only after the fact; the planned observability includes a duration watchdog, LIST/fold progress events, and an alert for an unbalanced `gc_fold_begin`/`gc_fold_end` pair.

`ca-gc-dryrun` systematically under-counted reachability relative to real GC and fsck, while real GC remained safe with zero dangling blobs; the intended invariant is `dryrun ⊆ (unreachable ∪ pending-gc)`.

The unmatched removal-fold `-1` is harmless under the current edge-set model because source edges are set membership keyed by `(ref, ManifestId, path)`, not a counter; erasing an already-absent edge cannot affect another manifest's edges.

A rebuild that condemns nothing cannot reclaim a blob whose manifest no longer exists anywhere in the pool because that blob has no row in the rebuilt baseline; such blobs remain fsck `unaccounted` until the R4 build/upload registry exists.

`Pool::beginPartWrite` has an allocate/register window in which a build can be allocated after a drop sweep snapshots `inflight_builds`, reviving an empty ownerless `Live` namespace that GC does not sweep.

The GC-side recovered-in-degree warning was often a false alarm caused by a dedup-adopt-versus-condemn TOCTOU: a writer adopted a blob after GC read it as not condemned, and GC then spared it after recovering the fresh edge.

The safe response to a GC post-CAS cleanup error is to retain leaked bodies for the orphan-manifest sweep rather than fail the already-committed decision; cleanup errors after `gc/state` CAS are data-safe but can redden the round.

A GC scheduler retry loop used a fixed interval without backoff, failure counting, or a circuit breaker, and `system.content_addressed_mounts` exposed only `last_success_age_seconds` for the resulting health state.
On a completely full target, a GC round that must write runs or seals can fail before its pre-CAS delete phase, so external headroom may be required before GC can reclaim anything.
The local staging write path has no free-space reservation or scratch filesystem guard, and stale `<rand>.tmp` files survive unclean restart because local scratch initialization has no sweeper.

A truncated blob can be admitted as a dedup hit because `PartWriteTxn::observeAndAdmit` checks only `hr.size >= blob_header_len` and does not compare the payload size with the caller's expected `source.size`.
`LocalObjectStorage` writes final blob keys with `O_TRUNC` and no atomic PUT semantics, so ENOSPC or termination can leave a partial body that a later `putIfAbsent` treats as an existing object.
The local or NFS backend is not safe for racy multi-writer put-if-absent use because it lacks the atomicity guarantees provided by S3 conditional PUTs.
Concurrent readers and writers of the same `detached/<part>` ref on local storage can observe a half-written object; S3 does not have this torn-read class because PUT completion is atomic.

`system.remote_data_paths` did not push down `WHERE disk_name = ...`, causing it to walk every disk and recursively LIST the shared CA-s3 ref namespace; the CA-s3 lane measured 872 LIST requests with 436 first-attempt timeouts.
The CA-s3 lane observed `ConnectionGroup: Too many active sessions in group Disk` with 10,400 active sessions against an 8,000 warning limit; the test output itself remained correct.
Azure real-store GC validation remained the last leg of the real-S3 reclaim release gate after AWS and GCS validation.
The LIST-consistency probe in `Cas::Probe` is load-bearing before LIST-derived discovery can be trusted on a store, because S3 LIST may omit a just-PUT key.
No CA code capped `s3_max_connections` to backend permits, leaving a risk of 503 and retry storms under high concurrency.

CA product operability still required a `SYSTEM` control surface for starting and stopping GC, putting a pool read-only, and running checks; product-side GC stop existed only as a soak-harness workaround.
A first-release CAS pool format needs a self-describing version breadcrumb, a format freeze, a durable roster, and rollout machinery for `max_content_addressable_pool_format`.
The CA feature needs a backup and restore runbook covering its operator procedures.
Current integration tests use MinIO, but the production gate requires RustFS coverage because production S3-compatible backends enforce conditional PUT.

Per-part and per-ref `system.*` views plus a top-down decode/traversal surface were still missing even though GC logs, the event log, `content_addressed_mounts`, and the ca-fsck/dryrun/rebuild/ca-inspect tools existed.

Existing tables need a migration path using `ALTER TABLE ... MOVE PARTITION` to repack onto a `content_addressed` disk, with a mixed-version rule of read-new-before-write-new and a fail-closed format self-check.
The server OOM finding of approximately 49 GiB RSS at hour four had not been reproduced after the streaming `putBlob` fix and required a long soak to confirm resolution.

One CAS pool is one trust domain: CityHash128 and XXH3 are not cryptographic and deduplication is cross-tenant within a pool; multi-tenant isolation requires cryptographic hashing or trust-domain-scoped deduplication.
Expedited or GDPR deletion is intended to confirm that no live ref remains under the GC lock and then bypass the normal two-phase graduation delay without changing the layout.
Content-addressed encryption deduplication is scoped per encryption key, with key-local hash derivation.

The ephemeral reader-pin design remains unimplemented because normal MergeTree part lifetime covers live refs and an absent live object already surfaces `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`; any ref-less or cross-node reader path must be audited first.
A read-path 404 currently surfaces as a hard error under INV-NO-DANGLE; auto-repair-on-404 remains only a resilience idea.

The proposed `ch128ctx` blob hash is `cityHash128(content) ∥ xxh3_64(part_name, file_name) ∥ size`, a 256-bit slot-bound digest intended to prevent cross-slot adversarial deduplication while preserving same-slot retry and replica-write deduplication.
`casPutObject` retries with the same frozen payload after a token conflict, so a future concurrent appender requires a real `casAppendObject` that re-reads base content inside the retry loop.
Out-of-band uploads under a staging prefix must be adopted through verified hash-then-publish copy-forward rather than trusted in place.
A CA write path can spill an entire 100 GiB merge to approximately 93 GiB of local scratch, so very large parts require streaming hash support or documented S3-native staging.
A shared-pool replica could re-merge and re-spill a deduplicated 100 GiB blob, consuming approximately 186 GiB of scratch across the two replicas.
A 20,000-column `OPTIMIZE FINAL` generated O(columns) S3 operations and stalled in an S3 retry storm.
A 256-partition insert took approximately 10 seconds because it performed O(partitions) CAS commits.
Starting a server with 10,000 tables required approximately 152,000 S3 operations for LISTs and GETs, while recovery remained fast.
A one-hour soak measured `pool_bytes` at approximately 400 times `logical_bytes`, attributed to RustFS overwrite-version retention and CA debris rather than a dangling-data safety issue.

The old CA Keeper `manifest_hash` proposal was rejected because it would couple replication to one disk implementation; fetch-by-relink learns the manifest id in-band and manifest divergence is a bounded dedup miss.
The per-namespace `RootShardManifest` model and `Store::shardOf` were replaced by per-table snapshot-plus-log state; root-shard-axis backlog items are obsolete.

The CA write path's allocation trace was dominated by `ContentAddressedTransaction::tryCreateWriteBuffer` and `writeFile`, while CPU traces were clean; the finding was allocation volume, not CPU or correctness.
The CA commit/ref-op path copied the whole `std::map<std::string, DB::Cas::RefCommittedRow>` `RefTableState` by value, creating O(refs) work per commit and O(refs·commits) over a workload.

The source-layout mechanical phase produced intermediate commits that were not clean-buildable because three external include fixes remained uncommitted; incremental-build success did not prove the committed tree built.

Moving a part to a `content_addressed` disk through `ALTER TABLE ... MOVE PART ... TO DISK 'ca'` used `promote` for the `moving` ref and failed the unique-ref invariant when `moving` already named another manifest.
A CA disk without an explicit scratch path creates `<data-path>/disks/<name>/cas_scratch/` at startup, and the parent `disks/` directory must be writable by the server user.

GC collapse under mass table drops was a queue-stability failure: serialized rounds became longer than the arrival rate, so dropped namespaces persisted, the universe grew, and subsequent folds became slower.

A regular GC round is all-or-nothing: `fold` produces one `gc/state` CAS followed by cleanup, and cleanup occurs only after the commit point because a durable `Removed` snapshot must precede deletion of covered logs.

The GC meta pool uses a queue of zero effective depth and `scheduleOrThrowOnError` blocks the fold thread from the 17th in-flight meta operation onward, preventing fold LIST/GET work from overlapping with condemn PUTs.
Completed namespaces retain `_cleanup` markers and their newest constant-size `Removed` snapshots, so the globally enumerated ref prefix grows linearly with historically unique namespaces.

In the measured CA-s3 CI run, 63% of ref-page volume was already-dropped namespaces: 97 of 128 namespaces had been dropped before the query began, and 9,538 of 15,123 namespaces were explicitly dropped.
A damaged `_ckpt` is isolated to a per-namespace hold, but that hold still shuts the round-wide destructive gate and `publishCkpt` has no repair path because it hits the same decode failure.
A naive GC fold budget is unsafe: omitted `+1` edges must suppress deletion rather than permit it, so bounded rounds require durable progress state.

The GC bottleneck study requires per-phase wall time, request counts by verb, bytes, pages, retries, and timeouts; it also requires a namespace-churn reproduction rig with controllable arrival rate and an unsaturated endpoint.

The GC/fsck disagreement was measured as 56 present blobs with no live reference, each carrying one residual source edge in the adopted in-degree run while GC marked zero candidates across 1,062 rounds.
`foldManifestEdges` returns false without deltas when a manifest body is absent, and the caller is intended to clamp the table rather than abort the round or advance its cursor.
An unmatched `-1` delta is silently ignored by the set-presence merge keyed by `(blob_ref, source_id)`, so its corresponding `+1` can remain forever and retain a blob until a full `ca-gc-rebuild`.
The retained-blob incident measured 56 blobs and 104,755 bytes over one four-hour soak; the leak rate was unbounded over time under the observed mechanism.

GC discovers ref-log transactions by paginating `LIST(cas/refs/)` without a snapshot token, high-water mark, or contiguity proof, and advances the cursor per fully folded log it happened to see; an omitted record is permanently skipped.

A skipped live manifest `+1` can cause exact-token deletion of a blob still referenced by that manifest after another owner's `-1` folds, because exact-token deletion protects against replacement but not an owner edge absent from GC state.

`DeleteObjects` cannot replace token-conditional `deleteExact` because bulk delete has no per-object precondition and could delete a replaced incarnation; parallel individual conditional deletes preserve exactness.

The chosen interim response to the LIST-hole hypothesis was mechanism-agnostic detection: compare two ref-prefix enumerations before advancing a cursor and compare intended-to-fold records with actually applied records; the permanent journal-chain fix remains required before release.
A missing sequence id is not itself anomalous because a pre-attempt refused append can leave a safe gap; an object that exists at or below the cursor but was never applied is the unambiguous anomaly.
An adopted fold seal once referenced a missing run under an older generation key, causing `zeroInDegree` to find no candidates and allowing GC to complete rounds while reclaiming nothing.

The holey-list sabotage configuration `_sab_holeylist` of `CaRelinkConfirmCore.tla` violated `ConfirmedRelinkNeverDangles` with one incomplete LIST page, proving that relink confirmation is safe only conditional on LIST completeness.
`ca-fsck` was deliberately kept non-fatal for `stale_edge` findings pending a separate retention-leak decision.
For S42, green means consistent on-disk and in-memory state; targeted poison/failpoint counters are reported rather than gating, while a generic allocation-fault anti-vacuity guard remains required.
Each GC phase is intended to emit its own row in `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`, with further study deferred until metrics from real runs exist.
Force-claiming an owner-absent pool root can lock the real server out, so operator recovery for a differing server UUID must distinguish post-mortem use from taking ownership from a live server.
The 600-second product fsck deadline was insufficient for a roughly 29 GiB pool: a measured run took 731.1 seconds and returned `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` without a `reachable=` line.
A 404,065-log GC round took 1,829.6 seconds for 3,420,091 serial requests, with the large-round cost near 0.5 ms per request.
On the largest measured round, edge HEADs accounted for approximately 1.5 million of 3.42 million requests, or 44% and about 800 seconds of serial time.
A round-scoped cache could remove 39.6% of manifest-body edge re-reads, measured at approximately 597,000 redundant edges and about 600 seconds on the 404,000-log round.
GC read parallelism is safe because tables fold independently and log reads can be prefetched while prior logs are applied; the ordering constraint applies to folding, not fetching.
Bulk deletion is rejected for GC because `deleteExact` must preserve token-conditional safety and report `TokenMismatch` without deleting the object when the token is wrong.
The S42 CI-scale run injected 2,184 allocation faults, observed zero `CasRefApplyPoisoned`, two wedged and two unwedged ref lanes, zero `CasRefAppendDefiniteFailure`, and 11,960 acknowledged blocks.

Under mass request timeouts, the write path returns `UNCERTAIN (retry budget exhausted)` and wedges affected ref lanes rather than guessing; the affected lanes can later unwedge without silent data loss.

Completed unfiltered `unit_tests_dbms` logs can contain NUL bytes and omit the beginning of redirected stdout; use `grep -a`, keep completion markers in a separate small file, and rely on the surviving gtest summary for totals.

The numbered CAS documents still describe pre-Stage-A namespace files as `roots/<ns>/_files/<name>` and refs as `cas/refs/<ns>/<shard>`; the documentation sweep should wait until Stage B key shapes settle.

A loose object at `roots/<srid>/_files/x` satisfies the current `parseNamespaceFileKey` condition and is classified as a corrupt namespace file, causing `ca-decommission` to refuse and `ca-fsck` to report a hard `lifeless_keys` finding even though the key need not represent damage.

A reachable state handled by code must not be guarded by `chassert`: the handler is the fail-closed behavior, and an assertion above it otherwise makes sanitizer/debug builds abort while release builds execute the handler.

When a function's returned aggregate element type, member count, or member order changes, every structured-binding call site such as `auto [a, b]` must be audited because C++17 can silently rebind fields without a compile error.
The `CasGcStopStart` suite passed standalone in 69 seconds but had a 60-second per-suite gate timeout, making the gate failure deterministic until the timeout, suite split, or runtime changes.

The CAS gate filter `Cas*:CA*` omitted `CaWiring`, `CaLifecycle`, several `RefWriter*` suites, and `RefTableCacheEviction`; twenty suites, including 17 CAS-relevant suites, were unclaimed by the gate.
`CasRefCatalog::resolveLifeOrSentinel` should return `std::optional<NamespaceLifeId>` rather than a plausible sentinel fallback so every caller must explicitly handle an unknown catalog life.
GC, fsck, decommission, probe, and rebuild paths must resolve namespace life once per run and thread that result instead of repeatedly re-deriving it from independent mechanisms.

The scalar `suppress_destructive = !anomalies.empty() || !holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete` gate lets one namespace's anomaly stop reclamation for the whole pool; the intended Stage B shape is a per-namespace destructive gate.

Deleting a never-born namespace's `_ckpt` from a `CORRUPTED_DATA` conflict path is unsafe because the conflict proves another object occupies the key, so the delete could remove a live successor's recovery checkpoint; a backstop must independently verify emptiness with a real LIST.
The pool-wide `content_addressed_s3/cas/ref_catalog` key accounted for 137 of 250 S3 timeout lines and 125 code-499 transient errors across 66 namespaces on the CA-s3 stateless lane.

The catalog's single-object atomicity makes every table creation contend on the same CAS target, turning high-rate table creation into timeout-prone serialization; reverting to unreliable pool LIST is not the accepted fix direction.
`Mode::Native` tests ignore the unique storage root and write keys into the process working directory, making their namespace shared across all Native tests in the binary.

The manifest-cleanup GC phase is a one-shot pipeline: its `-1` edge is consumed in the same CAS that produces `mf_cleanup`, so a per-round cap can permanently skip entries rather than defer them to the next intake.

A cap on manifest cleanup was rejected because it converted a bounded burst into a permanent leak; measured cap=5000 left 112,518 entries skipped, while disabling the cap drained 223,714 entries in-round.
After INV-4, each committed ref-log chunk pays a serial `GET _ckpt` plus token-CAS after the log PUT, so a lone INSERT pays four serial RTTs across its two ref transactions.
The ref durability order is `log PUT → _ckpt CAS → ack`, and retry-after-conflict must perform a whole-body exact re-read and re-merge regardless of the first-attempt `_ckpt` view policy.
Write-path stage 1 reduced CA wide-insert wall time from 58.41 seconds to 30.26 seconds and CA-vs-plain from 3.0x to 1.59x, while reducing top-thread Real share from 72.3% to 14.5%.

The transaction ordering invariant is per state domain: operations touching in-memory part staging dispatch eagerly, while the deferred queue is reserved for durable non-staging effects; a total order across both domains is impossible because read-your-writes and abort safety impose opposite requirements.

During sustained writes, `CasRefLedger::confirmExactRef` was available for approximately 17% of relink attempts, with about 92,000 refusals versus 19,531 proven confirmations in the measured sender lane.

A relink refusal is returned as retry-later `NETWORK_ERROR`; the replication queue requeues and reselects the fetch, and the receiver must not re-request bytes from the same source because that would be unsound.
`Store::resolveRef` hardcodes `.manifest_size = 0`, causing `PartFolderView::weight()` to undercount the manifest body because its weight is `bytes + manifest_size`.

The publish-confirm relink protocol publishes the receiver manifest and precommit first, then asks the sender's lane-linearized `confirmExactRef` about the exact `ManifestRef`, promoting only on a yes and retrying through the replication queue on no or unknown.
The mount-lease keeper can be silent at the default log level during a fence-to-remount episode, leaving renewal failure, fence arming, remount phases, and completion absent from the server log.
During the fence-to-remount window, durable writes return `668`/`210` immediately; converting short fence windows into bounded query-write waits requires an explicit write-path design decision.
